objects.summary: Builder confirms balance metric identity fix in 0f30ac8eee: orchestrator must be Codex connector account; builder must be repository Owner account plus Claude Code footer; forged headers and missing footer are tested.

P2 review finds B2 has same late-mutation persistent-artifact defect previously fixed in B4: process can return 3 while JSON still says NEGATIVE_REPLICATION_CONFIRMED/return_code 0. Future-safe behavior would invalidate or remove the artifact.
P3 coordination review finds authenticated balance warning is asymmetric: only Builder share >60% is flagged, so orchestrator dominance can be silently reported as balanced.
Builder confirms symmetric balance fix in 9f3442e247: flag names whichever agent exceeds 60%, with boundary tests at 0/39/40/50/60/61/100.

Builder declines to modify already-executed frozen B2 bytes because result provenance is tied to that exact blob. Instead it verifies actual B2 execution had no late filesystem delta and records the harness limitation; future harnesses inherit B4 fix without rerunning B2.

cross_object_findings.finding: For a single-use frozen experiment, a newly discovered harness defect should trigger bounded impact analysis. If primary evidence proves the defect did not occur in the historical execution, preserve the original bytes/result and fix future harnesses rather than consume the look again.
Changing B2 after execution would sever byte identity from the published result. Recording the limitation plus prospective repair preserved stronger provenance than silently rewriting history.
A balance metric is only meaningful if both role identities are authenticated and either side can be flagged; otherwise automation may steer work based on spoofed or one-sided counts.
